title: The Jet That Hugged the Wall — Canine Eccentric Coandă Mitral Regurgitation Jets (V015), 2D vs. 3D Echocardiography, EPIC Chamber Cutoffs & Focused Echo Agreement

teenKit.tldr: A tiny puppy's mysterious heart failure exposes a major flaw in medical imaging: blood leaks that stick to chamber walls hide their true danger from standard 2D scans. Solving this requires combining fluid physics, 3D cameras, and precise mathematical cutoffs.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that how we measure reality depends entirely on our tools, reminding us that even in high-tech medicine, what you see isn't always what's actually happening.
keyTakeaways: The Coandă effect causes fluid jets to cling to nearby surfaces, which tricks standard 2D color-flow ultrasound into underestimating how severe a heart valve leak really is.
A resting heart rate of 180 beats per minute in an 8-pound puppy is a flashing red siren indicating the body is frantically panicking to make up for lost oxygen.
Modern cardiology relies on advanced 3D imaging and strict mathematical cutoffs like the EPIC trial thresholds to turn fuzzy, subjective shadows into objective life-or-death decisions.

vocab.meaning: The physical tendency of a moving fluid or gas to stick to a nearby curved surface rather than shooting straight out.
A faulty heart valve that fails to seal tightly, allowing blood to squirt backward into the wrong chamber every time the heart beats.
An ultrasound scan of the heart that produces flat, two-dimensional slice images, making it easy to miss three-dimensional spatial details.
The narrowest, highest-velocity neck of a leaking fluid jet right as it shoots through a faulty valve opening.

quiz.question: Why did the 5-month-old puppy's heart rate skyrocket to 180 beats per minute?
options: She drank too much caffeine before arriving at the clinic.
Her sympathetic nervous system panicked to compensate for a massive drop in forward blood flow.
She was just playing too hard with the veterinary staff.
Her pacemaker malfunctioned during the physical exam.
quiz.explanation: When forward blood flow drops due to a leaky valve, adrenaline floods the body, forcing the heart to beat faster and faster to deliver enough oxygen.

quiz.question: What is the primary danger of a 'wall-hugging' Coandă jet in cardiac imaging?
options: It completely shatters the ultrasound probe with high-frequency sound waves.
It makes the heart stop beating instantly.
It tricks standard 2D color-flow mapping into underestimating the true severity of the leak.
It reverses the direction of blood flow throughout the entire body.
quiz.explanation: Because the leaking jet hugs the chamber wall, standard 2D color Doppler fails to capture its full area, making a dangerous leak look deceptively small.

quiz.question: Why do cardiologists use standardized clinical trials like EPIC instead of just guessing?
options: To eliminate observer variability and establish strict, evidence-based cutoffs for treatment.
To make medical textbooks thicker and harder to read.
Because insurance companies refuse to pay for creative thinking.
To prove that puppies are tougher than adult dogs.
quiz.explanation: Strict criteria like LA:Ao and LVIDdN thresholds remove human guesswork from fuzzy ultrasound scans so doctors can accurately time life-saving interventions.
